A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same heterogeneous recursive planning framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, added, and removed content to be matched reliably.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 report original narrative-generation and report-generation experiments, including ablations. Appendix A also reports baseline reproduction and configuration comparisons.

after.justification: Sections 6.1–6.2 retain the original experiments and add a LongReport human evaluation against Gemini Deep Research, with detailed results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The typed recursive decomposition and state-based DAG scheduling remain. However, v3 explicitly adds context retrieval and goal updating to Algorithm 1, while no longer stating v1's mandatory reasoning task after retrieval sequences. The PDFs do not establish whether these reflect procedural changes or expanded and condensed documentation of the existing implementation.

E1.justification: V3 adds LongReport: 12 detailed, time-sensitive prompts covering complex retrieval, information integration, and analytical writing, evaluated with reports exceeding 10,000 words. This substantially extends the task requirements beyond the retained TELL ME A STORY and WildSeek evaluations.

E2.justification: Gemini Deep Research with 2.5 Pro is added as the comparator in the new LongReport evaluation. E2E, Agent's Room, STORM, Co-STORM, and Perplexity Deep Research remain in their original comparisons; the appendix baseline variants are also retained.

E3.justification: The new LongReport study introduces a substantially different evaluation protocol: Gemini 2.5 Pro generation, five human annotators assessing every report pair, anonymous and randomized presentation, five rubric dimensions including clarity, and overall preferences. It also standardizes formatting and removes titles and report appendices, explicitly excluding citation-source fidelity. The original benchmark protocols are largely retained.

E4.justification: The recursion/type ablations, 2K–8K narrative-length analysis, and STORM/Co-STORM configuration comparisons are retained. Appendix B.4 adds case analyses of human judgments, including Gemini's incomplete report in Sample 7 and WriteHERE's very long but less-preferred report in Sample 6.

E5.justification: Appendix B introduces aggregation of five human ratings per report, reporting mean rubric scores and per-topic preference counts that expose annotator disagreement. The original 14-trial LLM judging and Davidson scoring remain unchanged. Neither version reports generation-seed variability, confidence intervals, or new significance tests.

E6.justification: The original numerical results are unchanged, including Tables 1–2 and v1 Tables 3–4, now v3 Tables 7–8. New LongReport results report WriteHERE/Gemini breadth scores of 4.5/4.2 and depth scores of 4.0/3.8. The reported 7:5 outcome counts topic-majority wins; individual preference votes total 30:30. Report-length statistics are added, while v1's generated DeepSeek R1 report example is removed.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 removes the input-output interface O from the formal agent-system tuple. V3 also omits the separately stated executability and goal-achievement conditions from Section 3.3, although these concepts remain elsewhere. The central planning formulation and typed-decomposition hypothesis are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a unified planning view of writing, heterogeneous recursive decomposition, adaptive task scheduling, and improved narrative/report quality over the original baselines. Naming the framework WriteHERE and adding supporting human evaluation do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds a qualified interpretation of the human study, describing comparable performance and differences in clarity versus breadth, depth, and novelty. It also adds process-diagnostic limitations and framework-specific qualifications about unreliable retrieved information, synthesis errors, and absent built-in debiasing. The earlier computational-efficiency and human-feedback limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands reproducibility documentation through memory/context-selection details, module descriptions, a worked execution trace, and narrative-generation prompts. These disclose atomicity guidance, task schemas, dependency rules, and planning constraints. It also specifies GPT-4o-mini for retrieval ranking/summarization and provides LongReport access information, evaluation rubrics, preprocessing instructions, and dataset licenses. These disclosures do not establish that existing settings changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix A substantially expand the relationship to classical HTN planning and modern reasoning frameworks. Added discussion covers systems such as NOAH, Nonlin, and SHOP, alongside ReasonFlux, Tree of Thoughts, CoR, and MetaGPT. V3 more carefully distinguishes hierarchical goal decomposition from reasoning-path exploration and credits the earlier Plan-and-Write work.

P1.justification: V3 reorganizes the method exposition into HRP and a dedicated WriteHERE framework section, rewrites and expands implementation explanations, and moves extended related work into Appendix A. The appendices are substantially restructured around human evaluation, implementation, a walkthrough, prompts, examples, risks, and licenses. The retained fiction example is relocated unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 adds an overview diagram as Figure 1, report statistics and human-result tables, detailed dataset tables, and formatted walkthrough and prompt boxes. Existing diagrams and benchmark displays are retained with renumbering, caption revisions, and layout adjustments; the original appendix comparison tables move to Tables 7–8.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses important validation and reproducibility gaps in v1 through blinded human assessment of extended reports and substantially fuller implementation instructions, prompts, and execution examples. These gains improve the paper beyond its unchanged automatic benchmark scores. The human evidence remains limited to 12 topics, excludes citation accuracy, and supports comparability rather than clear superiority: the 7:5 topic outcome corresponds to 30:30 individual votes. Those limitations temper the performance interpretation without outweighing the substantial documentation and validation gains.
